objective: Close the charter evolution loop as a standing monthly instrument: every clause a charter admits nothing enforces becomes a named harness task with an owner, every incident amends exactly one charter, and a changelog audit sends any clause cited by zero decisions in 30 days to review
rationale: The lab has run this loop end to end exactly once and has never run it as a loop. The 2026-08-08 arc is the proof that the shape works: an owner order in the morning became a lesson plus a verification charter revision, which became two audits, which became retroactive annotations, which became adopted enforcement machinery with a green suite, inside one day. What is missing is the standing version, and each of the three clauses is already measurable. First, the unenforced-clause half is not hypothetical: six of the nine charters carry an enforcement section that names its own gaps out loud, and those sections name 14 open clauses between them, among them the goals charter's axis B scores, axis C scores and prediction requirement, the escalation charter's unset free-spend thresholds and nightly band, the compute budget charter's measured-versus-estimated basis check, and the supervision charter's three unverified dispatch conditions. Nobody owns any of the 14 and none has a due date. Second, the one-incident-one-amendment half has no map at all; amendments land as version-bump prose at the head of each charter, with 12 labelled change paragraphs and the rest carried as unlabelled header text, and the only complete amendment trail is the commit history over the charters directory. Third, staleness is the cheapest of the three to start and the most likely to surprise: structured citations of the form charter-name plus section number appear about a dozen times in the whole record against roughly 117 charter sections, which is under 8 percent, and the honest reading is that the citation format is inconsistent rather than that the clauses are dead. That makes the first pass a format repair as much as an audit, and it should say so rather than declaring most of the charter estate dead. Axis A: a report-kind item at zero solver cost, so it ranks at the ranking floor. Axis B: 0, no wall row moves. Axis C: 0, no scored column is touched.
citations: The lab capability strategy, Katie's directive of 2026-08-08
The goals and research proposal charter, version 1.4, section 7
The case selection charter, version 1.3, sections 1 and 9
The charters index and its revision protocol
The lessons record, its 40 numbered lessons and the L-40 entry
The supervisor-maintained product list and its changelog
cost_basis: measured; the charters, their commit history and the docket decision trail are already on disk and the pass is a text sweep over them, so no solver time is spent and no case is opened
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes with a decision attached to each. One: the register closes at or near the 14 clauses the charters already admit, which converts a diffuse worry into a numbered backlog with owners and a monthly burn-down. Two: the sweep finds gaps the enforcement sections do not admit, which means the honesty lists themselves are stale and the charters owe a correction before anything else. Three: the staleness audit flags the overwhelming majority of sections, in which case the finding is about citation format rather than about dead clauses, the repair is a citation convention, and the audit is re-run against it before any clause is retired.
sequencing: Dispatchable now. Strategy rule 3 slow-burn, zero solver cost, subordinate to the Ladder V queue under rule 1 but competing for no compute with it.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Charter evolution loop: every charter's "nothing enforces this yet" clause becomes a harness task; every incident amends exactly one charter; changelog audit that no clause has gone stale (cited by zero decisions in 30 days -> review).' Operationalised as three tables per monthly pass. (a) The unenforced-clause register, complete over every charter, each row carrying an owner and a state; the pass fails if any charter is unswept. (b) The incident-to-amendment map, every root-caused incident of the period mapped to exactly one charter amendment, with unmapped incidents named rather than dropped. (c) The staleness list, every clause with zero citing decisions in the trailing 30 days, each dispositioned retire or re-apply, and no clause retired on the first pass while the citation format is still being repaired.
